title: Bali packing guide for women
description: What to wear in Bali: temples, Ubud, beach clubs and sunset bars for women. Packing lists by trip length, sarong rules and looks at three budgets.
intro: Bali is soft, green and humid. You will walk through rice terraces, visit temples, swim and watch the sunset. Pack light, flowy and quick-dry. Bring one sarong. Here are looks, a modesty note for temples and packing lists for three, five and seven days.

sections.heading: Temple note
sections.body: Bali temples ask you to cover your legs and your shoulders. Most sites lend or rent a sarong and a sash at the gate. Carry your own to save time. Wear a top with sleeves or a shawl. Do not enter a temple during your period, as this is a local custom. Be quiet and do not step over offerings on the ground. Remove shoes if asked.
tips: Carry a sarong and a sash.
Cover shoulders. A light shirt over a tank works.
Photos near prayer areas: ask first.

sections.heading: Outfit formulas
sections.body: Each with footwear and one accessory.

looks.name: Ubud day
pieces: Cotton midi dress, about ₹1,400 (H&M, Fabindia or Myntra)
Light linen shirt as a cover, about ₹900
looks.why: Cotton in a soft colour looks right among rice terraces.

looks.name: Beach club day
pieces: Swimsuit with a printed sarong, about ₹2,200 (Zara or H&M)
Linen shirt as a cover, about ₹1,800 (Uniqlo)
looks.why: The sarong works as a skirt, scarf and towel.

looks.name: Sunset bar
pieces: Satin slip dress or a printed wrap dress, about ₹3,500 (Mango, Zara or AND)
looks.why: Sunset is breezy, so a shawl is useful.

looks.name: Villa dinner
pieces: Silk or linen maxi dress, about ₹7,000 (Mango, Zara or Marks & Spencer)
looks.why: You look dressed without adding heat.

sections.heading: Packing list by trip length
sections.body: Three days: two sundresses, one swimsuit, one linen shirt, one sarong, one dinner dress, sandals and slides. Five days: add one more dress, one pair of shorts and a cover-up. Seven days: add a second swimsuit, a light jacket for volcano treks and a pair of trainers. Bali sells beautiful cotton dresses at low prices. Leave some room.
tips: Seven days: eleven or twelve items.
Pack a dry bag for the boat and beach days.

sections.heading: Moving around the island
sections.body: Bali is spread out. You will ride scooters, take cars and walk uneven paths. Plan for the way you move. If you ride a scooter, wear closed shoes and trousers, and carry a helmet. If you take a car, a dress is easy. If you walk the Campuhan ridge at dawn, wear sneakers and a light layer. In villages, wear a sarong over shorts. For a cooking class or a yoga class, pack a comfortable set. Bali has many yoga studios and they sell good leggings. Plan one outfit for every kind of day, and do not pack more than you need.
tips: Wear closed shoes on a scooter.
Carry a small waterproof bag for rain.
Pack a pair of leggings for yoga or class days.
Keep a light layer for air-conditioned cafes.

sections.heading: On the plane
sections.body: Wear loose trousers or leggings, a long tee and a cardigan. Compression socks help with long flights. You will land in warm, humid air, so keep a light layer on top that you can take off.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: April to October is dry and warm, with 27 to 31 degrees. November to March is wet and humid, with heavy afternoon rain. Pack quick-dry clothes and a rain jacket in the wet season. Volcano treks at dawn are cold. Pack a fleece.

sections.heading: Colour and silhouette
sections.body: Bali style is relaxed and natural. White, cream, sage, rust and indigo look right. Flowy silhouettes handle humidity. A smocked waist, a wrap or a drawstring helps shape without tightness. Colour wise, choose a base and an accent. Warm skin tones suit rust, olive and cream. Cool skin tones suit sage, soft blue and lilac.
tips: Choose a mix of two prints at most.
Keep jewellery light for the beach.

sections.heading: What to stop buying for Bali
sections.body: Stop buying heavy denim. Stop buying heels for cobbled paths and scooter rides. Stop buying delicate silk that will not survive humidity. Stop buying white shorts for scooter days. Buy a pair of good sandals and quick-dry dresses.

faq.q: What should women wear in Bali?
faq.a: Wear light, quick-dry dresses, shorts and sandals. Carry a sarong and a shawl for temples.

faq.q: Do I need to cover up in Bali?
faq.a: Yes at temples. Cover shoulders and legs. On beaches and at clubs, swimwear is fine.

faq.q: What should I wear for a scooter ride in Bali?
faq.a: Wear trousers or shorts over your swimsuit, closed shoes if you can and a helmet. A short skirt is risky on a scooter.

faq.q: How many dresses should I pack for a week?
faq.a: Four or five. Mix them with shorts, a shirt and a sarong.

cta.headline: Pack the colours that suit your skin
cta.sub: One selfie, five questions. See your season, your palette and your three strengths before you pack. Free.
